lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Compute two related integer/index items connected to fluency review and show a check for each.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: correct values with a verification step; weak answers omit checks or mishandle signs/brackets.

WATCH FOR
Skipping verification or misreading notation (especially negatives and indices).

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example for Fluency review: evaluate (−3)+7=4 and check by 4+(−7) returning −3, or use a number-line jump. Communicate each step.

TRY FIRST
Compute two related integer/index items connected to fluency review and show a check for each.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: correct values with a verification step; weak answers omit checks or mishandle signs/brackets.
teach_steps.explain:
Year 7 students develop fluency review with explicit methods, worked numerical examples and reasonableness checks. Represent the situation, choose an appropriate procedure, calculate carefully and verify with an inverse, estimate or diagram. Catalogue alignment uses MA4-ARI-C-01; detailed content-point mapping remains pending.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
